title: Fix: dedicated autoscaler priority routing drop during bursts + utilization reporting fixes
author: Marta Gonzalez
release_notes: Fixes a regression where priority routing + burst traffic could drop tokens and under-report utilization; improves autoscaler stability under mixed-priority workloads.
description:
Context: After the rollout of priority-aware routing for Dedicated fleets we observed intermittent throughput drops and incorrect utilization reporting when high-priority burst traffic coincided with medium-priority steady load. Root cause: a race in the priority routing enqueue/dequeue path combined with tokenbucket smoothing that could prematurely consume burst tokens for lower-priority work, and metrics code that aggregated utilization without accounting for transient burst lane allocations. This caused autoscaler decisions to undershoot and led to customer-visible latency spikes during bursts.

Summary of changes: 1) Fix race in priority-routing enqueue/dequeue by adding a lightweight per-lane lock-free admission check and moving token consumption to dequeue time when capacity is actually claimed. 2) Update tokenbucket smoothing algorithm to track burst-token reservations separately from steady-state tokens and expose new internal counters. 3) Adjust utilization reporting to emit lane-scoped metrics (dedicated.fleet.utilization{lane=}) and correct aggregation logic used by the autoscaler. 4) Add unit/integration tests that simulate mixed-priority burst scenarios and an e2e load test in perf-canary. 5) Add migration notes and a short compatibility shim to avoid double-counting in dashboards during rollout.

Commits (high level): - Fix priority enqueue/dequeue and add admission invariants (marta/prioritize-enqueue-fix) - Separate burst token reservations and smoothing math (marta/tokenbucket-burst-sep) - Expose lane-scoped utilization metrics and update autoscaler aggregation (marta/metrics-lane-scope) - Add tests and perf-canary job (marta/tests-priority-burst) - Changelog and release note (marta/changelog)

Files touched (high level): - redwood/serve/autoscaler/priority_router.go (core fix, 140 additions/30 deletions) - redwood/serve/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go (smoothing and burst reservation logic, 80 additions/20 deletions) - redwood/serve/metrics/utilization.go (lane-scoped metrics, 40 additions/25 deletions) - perf-canary/configs/priority-burst-test.yaml (new e2e) - redwood/tests/autoscaler/priority_burst_test.go (new unit/integration tests) - docs/release/notes/2025-10-15-autoscaler-priority-burst.md (release notes + rollout steps)

Testing & CI: Initial CI run failed on a flaky test in autoscaler simulation (test: TestPriorityEnqueueRace) that surfaced an ordering assumption in the test harness. I fixed the harness and re-ran. Full CI: unit tests, integration (simulator), lint, go vet, and perf-canary job. All checks passed on the final run (ci: pass). Perf-canary ran against a small dedicated fleet and showed 18% reduction in drop-rate and stable SLOs in the mixed-priority scenario.

Review conversation (summary): - Daniel Kim: requested clearer invariants for the admission path and suggested moving token consumption to dequeue (addressed in first commit). - Priya Shah: asked for explicit metric names and ensured Prometheus label usage was consistent with existing dashboards; asked to add migration notes (addressed). - Evan Liu: flagged potential contention on the new per-lane counters under extreme scale; we switched counters to sharded atomics to mitigate. - After two iterations and additional tests added to perf-canary, reviewers approved.

Backward compatibility & rollout: change is backwards-compatible; metrics include a compatibility shim that allows dashboards to show both old and new metrics for a short window. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets for 24h, monitor new lane-scoped metrics and autoscaler decision rates, then 50% for 48h before global. Release note included with recommended dashboard queries.

Merge: Squash merge performed by Priya Shah on 2025-10-15. Merge commit summary includes changelog and perf-canary results.

References: Linear ENG-7432 (autoscaler stability), ENG-7481 (observability improvements), incident SUP-4312 (customer report).
notes: Hotfix for an active regression; recommend backport to the most recent release branch if customers report similar symptoms.
